mainTopic: How a guardian's level of responsibility changes when his work, use or benefit ends, and when guarding counts as שמירה בבעלים.
overview: The משנה teaches that a craftsman is a שומר שכר over the item he works on. Once he says "טול את שלך והבא מעות", he becomes only a שומר חנם. The גמרא brings three versions of a discussion about whether simply saying "גמרתיו" works the same way, as רב חסדא holds; in each version the משנה is read so that it fits רב חסדא. In the third version, a borrower's liability on the return trip is limited to the loan period. אמימר rules that after the loan period the borrower is still a שומר שכר, because he had benefit, and a ברייתא about vessels sent to a father-in-law supports him. רב נחמן explains why a man trying to sell a donkey stays fully liable even on the way back. The גמרא then explains why "guard for me and I will guard for you" is not שמירה בבעלים: the guarding happens on different days. It ends with the story of the bakers and the stolen cloak, retold so that it fits both views on פשיעה בבעלים.

steps.title: Inference from the משנה: saying 'I finished it' leaves him a paid guardian
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's wording, the גמרא infers that a craftsman who only says "גמרתיו" is still a שומר שכר. That seems to contradict רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that if he only said "I finished it", he is still a paid guardian.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a "read-between-the-lines" inference from the משנה. The משנה said only "טול את שלך והבא מעות" makes him a שומר חנם, so a craftsman who merely said "גמרתיו" must still be a שומר שכר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said that "גמרתיו" is enough to lower the craftsman to a שומר חנם. The משנה named a stronger phrase, "take yours and bring money", as the point where he becomes a שומר חנם. So it sounds like anything weaker, such as "I finished", leaves him a שומר שכר, against רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: this implies / from here we infer (the opposite case)
"I finished it" (the craftsman announcing the work is done)
a paid guardian, who is responsible even for theft and loss

steps.confusionAlert: This step is only the inference part of a challenge against רב חסדא. The גמרא is not stating the final הלכה here.

phrases.english: This implies that "I finished it" leaves him a paid guardian.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge against רב חסדא that uses the משנה's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that "גמרתיו" makes the craftsman a שומר חנם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה gives "take yours and bring money" as the trigger. So the weaker phrase "I finished it" must leave him a שומר שכר.

steps.title: Rejecting the inference: the opposite case is 'bring money, then take yours'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the inference is wrong. The opposite case implied by the משנה is "bring money and then take yours", and that is where he stays a שומר שכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Rather, this implies that "Bring money and then take yours" leaves him a paid guardian.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא. It says the משנה is contrasting its case with a different one: a craftsman who says "bring money first, then take your item".
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key difference is the order of the words. "Take yours and bring money" lets the owner take the item now, so the craftsman is not holding it for himself. "Bring money and take yours" means he keeps the item until he is paid, so he is holding it for his own benefit and stays a שומר שכר. With this reading, the משנה says nothing about "גמרתיו".

keyTerms.meaning: "bring money and (then) take yours": the item is held until payment

phrases.aramaic: לָא, הָא ״הָבֵא מָעוֹת וְטוֹל אֶת שֶׁלְּךָ״
phrases.english: No. Rather, this implies that "Bring money and take yours"
leaves him a paid guardian.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, הָא ״הָבֵא מָעוֹת וְטוֹל אֶת שֶׁלְּךָ״ – שׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference of step 1 by offering a different implied opposite case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the specific inference about "גמרתיו", not the משנה itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's implied contrast is a change in word order ("bring money, then take"), not the phrase "I finished it".

steps.title: Challenge: then the משנה should have taught the simpler 'I finished it' case
steps.stepSummary: If "גמרתיו" also makes him a שומר חנם, the משנה should have taught that case. We would then know "take yours" is the same, through a כל שכן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about "I finished it": is he an unpaid guardian? If so, instead of teaching "All who said 'take yours and bring money' are unpaid guardians", let it teach us "I finished it". Then we would know all the more so for "take yours"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the defense. If "I finished it" already lowers him to a שומר חנם, why didn't the משנה teach that bigger news?
steps.deeperAnalysis: "גמרתיו" is the weaker release statement, and "טול את שלך" is the stronger one. If the weaker statement already makes him a שומר חנם, then the stronger one obviously does too (כל שכן). A משנה normally teaches the case that gives us the most information, so choosing "take yours" suggests "I finished it" is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: an unpaid guardian, responsible only for negligence

phrases.english: But "I finished it": what? Is he an unpaid guardian?
If so,
instead of teaching "And all those who said

phrases.aramaic: טוֹל אֶת שֶׁלְּךָ וְהָבֵא מָעוֹת – שׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם״,
phrases.english: 'Take yours and bring money' are unpaid guardians",
let it teach us "I finished it",
and all the more so "Take yours"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the defense in step 2 by asking why the משנה chose the less informative case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that "גמרתיו" makes him a שומר חנם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה should teach the bigger news, the weaker phrase. The stronger phrase would then follow by כל שכן.

steps.title: Answer: 'Take yours' had to be taught so we don't think he has no responsibility at all
steps.stepSummary: The משנה needed to teach "טול את שלך". Otherwise we might think that after saying it, the craftsman is not even a שומר חנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Take yours" needed to be taught. You might have thought he is not even an unpaid guardian; it teaches us that he is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The "take yours" case teaches something new in the other direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying "take yours" might seem to end all of the craftsman's responsibility. You might think he becomes no guardian at all. The משנה teaches that he is still at least a שומר חנם, so the case was not wasted even if "גמרתיו" also lowers him.

keyTerms.meaning: it was needed (for its own lesson)
it would enter your mind to say (a mistaken first thought)

steps.whatToRemember: In the first version, the משנה does not disprove רב חסדא. "Take yours" is taught to show he keeps at least שומר חנם responsibility, not to exclude "I finished it".

phrases.english: "Take yours" was needed.
It would enter your mind to say:
he is not even an unpaid guardian,
so it teaches us that he is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 by giving "take yours" its own lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: After "take yours", the craftsman has no responsibility at all.

steps.title: Second version: רב נחמן בר פפא brings the משנה as support
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רב נחמן בר פפא uses the משנה to support רב חסדא. He suggests that "גמרתיו" is the same as "טול את שלך".
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רב נחמן בר פפא said: We also learned this: "All those who said 'take yours and bring money' are unpaid guardians." Isn't the same true for "I finished it"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of the discussion. Here the משנה is used as a proof for רב חסדא instead of a challenge against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן בר פפא reads the משנה broadly. It mentions "take yours", but the same idea of the work being done should apply to "I finished it". That would fit רב חסדא's ruling that "גמרתיו" makes him a שומר חנם.

keyTerms.meaning: some say (a second version of the discussion)
we too have learned it (in a משנה)
is it not? (introducing a proposed proof)

phrases.english: Some say:
Rav Nachman bar Pappa said:
We too have learned this:
phrases.notes: "This" means רב חסדא's ruling that "I finished it" makes him an unpaid guardian.

phrases.aramaic: וְכוּלָּן שֶׁאָמְרוּ ״טוֹל אֶת שֶׁלְּךָ וְהָבֵא מָעוֹת״
phrases.english: "And all those who said 'Take yours and bring money'
are unpaid guardians."
Is it not that the same is true for "I finished it"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a second version where the same משנה supports רב חסדא instead of challenging him.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's ruling that "גמרתיו" makes the craftsman a שומר חנם
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: "וכולן שאמרו טול את שלך והבא מעות – שומר חנם"

steps.title: Rejecting the proof: 'take yours' is a special case
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. "טול את שלך" is different, so we cannot learn "גמרתיו" from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. "Take yours" is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב נחמן בר פפא's proof. The משנה's case cannot be stretched to cover "I finished it".
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Take yours" is an active handing back of the item, which is stronger than just announcing the work is done. So the משנה might apply only to that strong phrase, and it gives no proof for "גמרתיו". רב חסדא's ruling is not disproved, but it is not proven from the משנה either.
steps.whatToRemember: In both versions the משנה ends up neutral about "גמרתיו". It neither disproves nor proves רב חסדא.

phrases.english: No. "Take yours" is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not רב חסדא's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: "Take yours" is a stronger release statement than "I finished it", so we cannot learn one from the other.

steps.title: A third version: the craftsman's case from our משנה
steps.stepSummary: הונא מר בר מרימר brings the משנה that 'take yours and bring money' makes the craftsman a שומר חנם. He assumes 'גמרתיו' works the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: הונא מר בר מרימר, in front of רבינא, set two משניות against each other and resolved it. We learned: anyone who says 'Take yours and bring money' is a שומר חנם. And the same is true for 'I finished it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a third version of the discussion. This step only sets up the first side of a contradiction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'גמרתיו' is simply assumed to equal 'טול את שלך', the same view as רב חסדא. Once the work is done, the craftsman's responsibility drops from שומר שכר to שומר חנם. This drop is what will clash with the borrower's case.

keyTerms.meaning: He set the משניות against each other (he pointed out a contradiction)
An unpaid guardian, who is liable only for carelessness
'I finished it' (the craftsman's announcement that the work is done)

phrases.aramaic: הוּנָא מָר בַּר מָרִימָר קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבִינָא
phrases.english: Huna Mar bar Mareimar, before Ravina,
set the mishnayot against each other and resolved it.
We learned: And all those who said

phrases.aramaic: ״טוֹל אֶת שֶׁלְּךָ וְהָבֵא מָעוֹת״ – שׁוֹמֵר חִנָּם.
phrases.english: "Take yours and bring money" are an unpaid guardian.
And the same is true for "I finished it."

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּנָא מָר בַּר מָרִימָר קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבִינָא רָמֵי מַתְנִיתִין אַהֲדָדֵי וּמְשַׁנֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third version of the discussion, in which 'גמרתיו' is assumed to equal 'טול את שלך'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the craftsman says 'take yours' (and also 'גמרתיו'), he is only a שומר חנם.

steps.title: The borrower stays liable even while returning
steps.stepSummary: A different משנה says a borrower is liable if the animal dies on the way to him, and also on the way back. So his responsibility does not drop when his use ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he set it against this: if the borrower said 'Send it,' and the lender sent it and it died, the borrower is liable. The same is true when he returns it.
steps.whatsHappening: הונא מר brings the other side of the contradiction. A borrower stays fully liable even on the return trip, after he has finished using the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The craftsman's level of responsibility drops once his work is finished. The borrower's level of responsibility does not drop once his use is finished. Why should the two cases be different?

keyTerms.meaning: And he set against them (introduces the contradicting source)
A borrower, who is liable even for accidents
At the time he returns it

phrases.english: And he set against it: If the borrower said to him "Send it,"
and he sent it and it died, he is liable.
And so too when he returns it.
phrases.notes: He means that if the animal dies on the way back to the owner, the borrower is still liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the contradicting משנה against the craftsman's case in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a guardian's liability drops once his use or work is finished.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The craftsman goes down to שומר חנם after the work, yet the borrower keeps full liability even on the way back.

steps.title: Liable only during the loan period
steps.stepSummary: Using רב חסדא's rule, the borrower is liable on the return trip only if he returns the animal within the loan period. After the loan period, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: He resolved it, as רפרם בר פפא said in the name of רב חסדא: this was taught only when he returned it within the loan period. But after the loan period, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The contradiction is resolved. The borrower's extra liability lasts only while the loan period is still running.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Inside the loan period, he is still a borrower even on the way back, so he is liable. Once the loan period ends, his time of use is over, just like the craftsman whose work is done. So both cases follow the same idea.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only (in this case)
The days of its loan (the loan period)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next question: how far does that exemption go?

phrases.aramaic: וּמְשַׁנֵּי, אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: And he resolved it: Rafram bar Pappa said that Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁהֶחְזִיר בְּתוֹךְ יְמֵי שְׁאֵילָתָהּ,
phrases.english: They taught this only when he returned it within the days of its loan,
but after the days of its loan, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְשַׁנֵּי, אָמַר רַפְרָם בַּר פָּפָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the second משנה to a specific case (within the loan period).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The borrower is always liable on the return trip.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is liable only within the loan period. After it ends, he is exempt, like the craftsman after the work is done.

steps.title: Exempt completely, or still a paid guardian?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'exempt' means for a borrower returning after the loan period. Is he still liable as a שומר שכר, or not even that?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: is he exempt only from a borrower's liability but still liable as a שומר שכר? Or maybe he is not even a שומר שכר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רב חסדא's word 'exempt'. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A borrower is liable even for accidents. Losing that status could leave him as a שומר שכר, who is liable for theft and loss. Or it could leave him with even less responsibility.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them (a question that needs resolving)
A paid guardian, who is liable for theft and loss but not for accidents

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
Is he exempt as a borrower but liable as a paid guardian,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִּלְמָא שׁוֹמֵר שָׂכָר נָמֵי לָא הָוֵי?
phrases.english: or perhaps he is not even a paid guardian?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far רב חסדא's exemption from step 9 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a borrower returning after the loan period still has the liability of a שומר שכר.

steps.title: אמימר: he had benefit, so he must give benefit
steps.stepSummary: אמימר rules that he is exempt as a borrower but liable as a שומר שכר. Since he benefited from the animal, he must guard it well in return.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: it makes sense that he is exempt as a borrower but liable as a שומר שכר, since he had benefit, he must give benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר answers the question. The returning borrower is still a שומר שכר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower enjoyed the use of the animal. Because of that, it is fair that he gives something back by guarding it on the way home at the level of a paid guardian. He is not liable for accidents, but he is liable for theft and loss.

keyTerms.meaning: Since he benefited, he must give benefit

steps.whatToRemember: A borrower who returns an animal after the loan period is no longer liable for accidents. He is still a שומר שכר, because he had benefit from it.

phrases.english: Ameimar said: It stands to reason
he is exempt as a borrower and liable as a paid guardian,
since he benefited, he must give benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is exempt as a borrower but liable as a שומר שכר, because he had benefit.

steps.title: Support from the vessels sent to the father-in-law
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that someone who takes vessels on approval for his in-laws is liable for accidents on the way there. On the way back he is exempt for accidents, because he is like a שומר שכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports אמימר. Someone took vessels from a craftsman to send to his father-in-law and said: 'If they accept them, I'll pay their price. If not, I'll pay you for the benefit I got from them.' If the vessels were destroyed by accident on the way there, he is liable. On the way back, he is exempt, because he is like a שומר שכר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches אמימר's ruling. Even after his benefit is over, the man still has the level of a שומר שכר on the way back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the way there, he is fully responsible, even for accidents. On the way back, his benefit is finished, but he does not drop below a שומר שכר. That is exactly אמימר's point.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא teaches in line with him
The small benefit-value he gets from the vessels
They were destroyed by an accident beyond his control
The trip there / the trip back

steps.confusionAlert: 'Exempt' on the way back means exempt only for accidents. He is still liable for theft or loss, like any שומר שכר.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא backs up אמימר: someone whose benefit has ended still keeps the responsibility of a שומר שכר.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita in line with Ameimar:
One who takes vessels from the craftsman's house
to send them to his father-in-law's house,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר לוֹ: אִם מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתָן מִמֶּנִּי –
phrases.english: and said to him: If they accept them from me,
I will give you their price,
and if not, I will give you
according to the benefit I got from them,
phrases.notes: Even if they send the vessels back, he gained something by being seen to offer a gift, so he pays for that.

phrases.english: and they were destroyed by accident on the way there, he is liable,
on the way back, he is exempt,
because he is like a paid guardian.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that supports אמימר's answer in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: אמימר's ruling that after the benefit ends, a person is still a שומר שכר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the vessels taken from the craftsman's house for the father-in-law.

steps.title: The donkey taken to be sold and injured on the way back
steps.stepSummary: A man takes a donkey to sell at another place and will return it if it doesn't sell. It doesn't sell, and on the way back it is injured by an accident. רב נחמן rules that he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man got a donkey from his friend and said: I'll take it to a certain place. If it sells, good. If not, I'll bring it back to you. It didn't sell, and on the way back the donkey had an accident. The case came to רב נחמן, and he made the man pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case. רב נחמן rules that the man must pay for an accident that happened on the way back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This looks like the ברייתא from step 12, where the return trip is treated like a שומר שכר and accidents are exempt. But רב נחמן makes this man liable even for an accident on the return trip, so a clash is coming.

keyTerms.meaning: It suffered an אונס, an accident beyond his control

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּזַבֵּין לֵיהּ חֲמָרָא לְחַבְרֵיהּ,
phrases.english: There was a certain man who sold a donkey to his fellow,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: קָא מַמְטֵינָא לַיהּ לְדוּכְתָּא פְּלוֹנִי,
phrases.english: He said to him: I am bringing it to such-and-such a place;
phrases.notes: The one speaking is the man who received the donkey.

phrases.english: if it gets sold, good,
and if not, I will bring it back to you.
He went, and it was not sold,
and while he was coming back, it was injured in an accident.
He came before רב נחמן, who held him liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא גַּבְרָא דְּזַבֵּין לֵיהּ חֲמָרָא לְחַבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case that looks similar to the ברייתא in step 12 but gets a stricter ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who takes a donkey to try to sell it is liable for an accident even on the way back.

steps.title: רבה challenges רב נחמן from the ברייתא about the return trip
steps.stepSummary: רבה cites the ברייתא: on the way back the person is exempt from accidents because he is like a שומר שכר. So why did רב נחמן make this man pay?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה objected to רב נחמן: we learned that if the items had an accident on the way there, he is liable, but on the way back he is exempt, because he is like a paid guardian.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks רב נחמן's ruling using the ברייתא from step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the return trip is only like a שומר שכר, who does not pay for accidents. The donkey's accident happened on the way back, so by the ברייתא the man should be exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him from a source
A paid guardian, the same as a שומר שכר

phrases.english: רבה raised an objection to רב נחמן:
If they met with an accident on the way there, he is liable,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא from just before, about vessels taken on approval to show the in-laws.

phrases.english: and on the way back, he is exempt,
because he is like a paid guardian!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 13 using the source from step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that the man is liable for the accident on the way back
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats the return trip like a שומר שכר, who is exempt from accidents, so this man should be exempt too.

steps.title: For this man, the trip back still counts as the trip there
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that this man's return trip is really part of his use. Even on the way back, he would have sold the donkey if he found a buyer.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: for this man, the way back counts as the way there. Why? It's simple logic. On his way back, if he had found someone to buy it, wouldn't he have sold it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבה by showing that this case is different from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the use ends once the in-laws have seen the vessels, so the trip back is just returning them. Here the man is still trying to sell the donkey the whole way home. So he is still using it, and he keeps the full liability of a borrower until he gives it back.
steps.whatToRemember: The return trip is treated like a שומר שכר only when the use has really ended. If the person is still using the item on the way back, he stays fully liable.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזָרָה דְּהַאי – הֲלִיכָה הִיא.
phrases.english: He said to him: the way back of this one counts as the way there.
What is the reason? It is logic:
on his way back, if he had found a chance to sell it,
wouldn't he have sold it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: חֲזָרָה דְּהַאי – הֲלִיכָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's challenge by showing how the donkey case differs from the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every return trip is like a שומר שכר, so the man should be exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: Here the use continues on the way back, so the trip back is like the trip there and he is liable.

steps.title: The משנה: guarding for each other makes each a paid guardian
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: if one person says 'guard for me and I will guard for you,' each one is a שומר שכר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Guard my things for me, and I will guard yours for you': each one is a paid guardian.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up a question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each person is 'paid' by getting guarding service in return, so each one counts as a שומר שכר.

keyTerms.meaning: Guard for me and I will guard for you

phrases.english: "Guard for me and I will guard for you": a paid guardian.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section by quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Exchanging guarding makes each person a שומר שכר.

steps.title: Isn't this guarding while the owner is working for him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why each one is liable at all. Each is guarding while the owner is busy doing work for him, which is שמירה בבעלים, and that exempts a guardian.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? This is guarding with the owners!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner is working for the guardian while the guardian is guarding, the guardian is exempt. Here each person is guarding for the other, so it seems that each owner is 'working for' his guardian, and neither should be liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Guarding while the owner is working for the guardian, which exempts the guardian

phrases.english: But why? It is guarding with the owners!
phrases.notes: He means: the owner is busy helping the guardian at the same time, and in that case a guardian doesn't pay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that each person is a liable שומר שכר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each owner is serving his guardian at the same time, which is שמירה בבעלים, so the guardian should be exempt.

steps.title: רב פפא: the guarding happens on different days
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the משנה means: guard for me today, and I will guard for you tomorrow. When each one is guarding, the owner is not working for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the case is where he told him, 'Guard for me today, and I will guard for you tomorrow.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by explaining the exact case the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמירה בבעלים only applies if the owner is working for the guardian at the same time as the guarding. If the two people take turns on different days, then on each day the owner is not working for his guardian. So each one stays a liable שומר שכר.
steps.whatToRemember: 'Guard for me and I will guard for you' makes each one a שומר שכר because the guarding happens on different days, so it is not שמירה בבעלים.

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
It is where he said to him: "Guard for me today,
and I will guard for you tomorrow."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17 by narrowing the case in the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both people guard at the same time, so it is שמירה בבעלים and both are exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: They guard on different days, so it is not שמירה בבעלים and each is a liable שומר שכר.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists four swap deals that make each side a paid guardian
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that any trade of guarding or lending makes both sides שומרי שכר for each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'Guard for me and I will guard for you,' 'Lend to me and I will lend to you,' 'Guard for me and I will lend to you,' 'Lend to me and I will guard for you.' In all of these, each one becomes a paid guardian for the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that widens the משנה's case. It covers lending as well as guarding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in step 16 only mentioned guarding for guarding. This ברייתא adds that lending counts as payment too. Whatever favor a person gets back in return makes him a paid guardian.

keyTerms.meaning: Paid guardians, who are liable for theft and loss

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a repeat of step 16 by accident. The ברייתא is a different source that adds new cases, so the גמרא asks its question again.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'Guard for me and I will guard for you,'
'Lend to me and I will lend to you,'
'Guard for me and I will lend to you,'
'Lend to me and I will guard for you' –

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלָּן נַעֲשׂוּ שׁוֹמְרֵי שָׂכָר זֶה לָזֶה.
phrases.english: they all become paid guardians for each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that widens the משנה discussed in steps 16-18
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In any swap of guarding or lending, each side is a שומר שכר for the other.

steps.title: Why are they liable if the owner is working for the guardian?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question it asked about the משנה: this looks like שמירה בבעלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? It is guarding while the owner is with him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. While one person guards, the other is doing a favor for him, so the guardian should be exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A guardian is exempt when the owner is working for him during the guarding. In a swap deal it looks like both favors happen together. That would make it שמירה בבעלים and cancel liability.

keyTerms.meaning: Guarding while the owner is working for the guardian, which exempts him

phrases.english: But why?
It is guarding with the owners!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that both sides are liable as שומרי שכר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two favors seem to happen at the same time, which is שמירה בבעלים, and that exempts a guardian.

steps.title: רב פפא: the favors are on different days
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא again explains that the deal is 'today for me, tomorrow for you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is where he said to him, 'Guard for me today and I will guard for you tomorrow.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question the same way he did in step 18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the favors happen on different days, then while one person guards, the owner is not working for him. So it is not שמירה בבעלים, and the guardian is a liable שומר שכר.
steps.whatToRemember: A swap of favors makes both sides שומרי שכר, as long as the favors are not done at the same time.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It is where he said to him:
'Guard for me today
and I will guard for you tomorrow.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both favors happen at the same time, so it is שמירה בבעלים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The favors are on separate days, so the owner is not working for the guardian while he guards.

steps.title: The story of the bakers and the stolen cloak
steps.stepSummary: A group took turns baking. One asked the others to guard his cloak, it was stolen through their carelessness, and רב פפא made them pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were some dealers in ice plants, and every day one of them baked for the group. One day they told one of them, 'Go bake for us.' He said, 'Guard my cloak for me.' Before he returned, they were careless with it and it was stolen. They came before רב פפא, and he made them liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real case that tests the rule about guarding while the owner is working for you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cloak's owner was baking for the group while they guarded his cloak. רב פפא still ruled that they must pay, which looks like it goes against the idea of בבעלים.

phrases.english: There were certain ice-plant dealers

phrases.aramaic: דְּכֹל יוֹמָא הֲוָה אָפֵי לְה[וּ] חַד מִינַּיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: where every day one of them would bake for them.
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected wording, making it 'for them.'

phrases.english: One day
they said to one of them:
Go bake for us.
He said to them:
Guard my cloak for me.
Before he came back, they were careless with it
and it was stolen.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording is in square brackets. Both mean 'it was stolen.'

phrases.english: They came before Rav Pappa,
and he made them liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ אַהֲלוֹיֵי דְּכֹל יוֹמָא הֲוָה אָפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story about רב פפא that applies the topic of guarding while the owner is working
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא made the guardians pay for the stolen cloak.

steps.title: The רבנן challenge רב פפא: this is carelessness while the owner works
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן object that the owner was baking for them, so it is פשיעה בבעלים, and רב פפא is embarrassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to רב פפא: Why did you make them pay? It is carelessness while the owner is with them! He was embarrassed.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן attack רב פפא's ruling, and he seems to have no answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While they guarded the cloak, its owner was baking for them. The רבנן assume that פשיעה בבעלים exempts the guardians even though they were careless. רב פפא's embarrassment shows that he accepted the challenge. Step 25 points out that not everyone holds this way.

keyTerms.meaning: Carelessness by a guardian while the owner is working for him

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Rav Pappa:
Why?
It is carelessness with the owners!
He was embarrassed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן לְרַב פָּפָּא: אַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's ruling in the story
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's ruling that the guardians must pay
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The owner was baking for the guardians at the time, so the exemption of בבעלים should apply.

steps.title: It turns out the owner was drinking beer, not baking
steps.stepSummary: Later it came out that at the time of the theft the owner was drinking beer, so he was not working for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the end it came to light that at that time he was drinking beer.
steps.whatsHappening: New facts come out that defend רב פפא's ruling after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption of בבעלים only works if the owner is actually working for the guardian at that moment. Since he was drinking beer and not baking, the exemption did not apply, so רב פפא was right to make them pay.

phrases.english: In the end the matter came to light
that at that time
he was drinking beer.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the cloak's owner, who was supposed to be baking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב פפא against the challenge of step 23
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The owner was baking for them while they guarded, so they are exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was drinking beer at that moment, so he was not working for them and they are liable.

steps.title: Why the embarrassment, according to the view that carelessness with the owner is liable?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the story fits the view that פשיעה בבעלים is exempt. According to the view that it is liable, there was no reason for רב פפא to be embarrassed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says carelessness with the owners is exempt; that is why he was embarrassed. But for the one who says he is liable, why was he embarrassed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the way the story was told, using the מחלוקת about פשיעה בבעלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some hold that a guardian who is careless is liable even when the owner is working for him. According to them, the רבנן's complaint was not a real problem. So רב פפא should not have been embarrassed at all.

keyTerms.meaning: This works for the one who says

phrases.english: This works for the one who says
carelessness with the owners is exempt –
that is why he was embarrassed.
But for the one who says he is liable –
why was he embarrassed?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר פְּשִׁיעָה בִּבְעָלִים פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the story as told in steps 22-24
steps.kashyaTarget: The detail that רב פפא was embarrassed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If פשיעה בבעלים is liable, the רבנן's objection fails, so there was nothing to be embarrassed about.

steps.title: The story retold: guarding the cloak was his payment for baking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא retells the story. It was not his turn to bake, and he asked them to guard his cloak as payment for baking.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, that day was not his turn. They said to him, 'You go bake for us,' and he said to them, 'As payment for my baking for you, guard my cloak.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes how the story happened, so that it fits even the view that פשיעה בבעלים is liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, he baked on a day that was not his turn, and their guarding was paid for by his baking, so they were שומרי שכר. A שומר שכר pays for theft even without carelessness. So the רבנן's objection can be read as שמירה בבעלים, which exempts according to everyone, and that is why רב פפא was embarrassed even according to the view that פשיעה בבעלים is liable.
steps.whatToRemember: In the retold story, the guarding was paid for with baking, so the guardians were שומרי שכר. The objection then concerns שמירה בבעלים, which exempts according to everyone. That is why the story works for both views on פשיעה בבעלים.

phrases.english: Rather, that day
was not his turn,
and they said to him:
You go bake for us,
and he said to them:
As the payment for my baking for you,
guard my cloak.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָהוּא יוֹמָא לָאו דִּידֵיהּ הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25 by retelling the facts
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retelling the facts of the story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It was his regular turn to bake, and the only question was whether it was בבעלים.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was not his turn, and guarding the cloak was his payment for baking, so they were שומרי שכר.
